notToBeConfusedWith.name: Brandy
notToBeConfusedWith.note: The general category. Cognac is brandy made from grapes grown around the French town of Cognac and distilled twice in copper pot stills under its own legal designation.

generalSubstitutes.note: Grain rather than grape, and drier — a drink built on cognac's fruit and oak reads leaner and more spirit-forward with bourbon in its place.

forms.label: Standard strength
forms.sourceNote: USDA's Survey (FNDDS) record for brandy gives 231 kcal/100 g with no carbohydrate, sugar or fat, and 33.4 g alcohol per 100 g but no usable liquid density to turn that into an ABV, so the strength here is stated from Cognac's legal minimum bottling proof of 40% rather than derived from the record. Public domain. No measured liquid density is published anywhere in this record; the density-classes.json 'spirit-40' class is taken as the nearest fit and marked estimated.
